1.

Though Adam’s fall dishonoured God and brought us into need, Christ now has made atonement, vanquished sin and death indeed. His life glorified God, He died as sacrificial Lamb, Both mercy-seat and priest He became, and salvation for us won.

2.

Though sin has overflowed and reigned through death in might, Yet grace has overflowed the more, far more than sin’s dark blight. We died with Christ from its dominion, in His life we rose, Our bondage-service now is o’er, for Christ has made us free.

3.

Now God invites all peoples to His salvation, full and free, And calls each blessed who on Jesus wholly trusts indeed. So we sing and praise our God for what in faith we’ve gained; For grace and peace and glory are our portion evermore.

4.

The law can rule no more, for now is grace’s day; In Christ Jesus I am free from sin and death’s array. We died to sin and its service, to God we live may we; Great power o’er sin is found therein—to reckon constantly.

5.

Though “no good thing” in flesh doth dwell, yet Jesus bore its doom. We find no strength in self at all, but Scripture makes it known, That now the Spirit is our strength, that Christ in us doth dwell. To sons God hath exalted us! O what grace doth excel!

6.

Our God is “for us” on our way, who can against us stand? Soon we shall be like Christ Himself, for God hath so ordained; He intercedes for us with God, our Surety is He, From love so unspeakably great none e’er can part us free.
